Naomi / Laura — quick product assessment below. See attached draft 'kv-cache-segmentation.pdf' for a short technical note we can share if helpful.

Summary (can be used in customer-facing text):
- Per-tenant KV-cache namespaces: our runtime already isolates KV cache by customer and model instance. Keys are namespaced; there is no shared in-memory cache across tenants. This prevents accidental cross-tenant key collisions.
- Retention: snapshots are ephemeral by default, rotated continuously. We can implement a 30-day retention window for BrightWave as an operational configuration on their Dedicated/Private deployment or as a contract-limited feature in Hosted with a specific flag. For Hosted customers we will:
  * create a time-based lifecycle policy scoped to their tenant namespace,
  * surface retention as a configurable parameter in the account settings, and
  * document the operational process for snapshot deletion.
- Edge cases: if a customer pins model versions with persistent KV prepopulated across rollouts, some entries may be rehydrated — we'll document and mitigate by ensuring retention policies apply to rehydration paths as well.

Impact / timeline:
- For Dedicated/Private: we can turn on 30-day retention immediately with a config change; no infra changes needed.
- For Hosted: engineering needs ~2–3 weeks to add tenant-scoped retention UI + automation to guarantee deletion (we can provide an interim contract commitment and operational runbook within 3 business days).

Suggested customer language (one-paragraph to include in the cover response):
"Redwood confirms TelemetryStream may be added as a subprocessor for telemetry related to inference routing. Our runtime enforces per-customer KV-cache namespaces so data is isolated by tenant. For BrightWave we will apply a tenant-scoped 30-day snapshot retention policy; snapshots are encrypted at rest. For Hosted customers, we will provide an interim operational commitment while we complete UI/automation work (target completion in ~3 weeks)."

Attachments: kv-cache-segmentation.pdf (internal technical note).

—Grace
Director, Product Management — Serving Runtime

Naomi/Laura/Grace — Security assessment and conditional signoff below. Short version: acceptable with KMS & audit commitments.

Findings and conditions:
- Subprocessor addition: TelemetryStream is acceptable provided:
  1) TelemetryStream attests to SOC2 Type II or equivalent and provides the signed SSAE/SOC report (we can accept in lieu of on-site audit) — ask Legal to request TelemetryStream_SA.pdf + latest report.
  2) Contract includes right to periodic security attestation and breach notification timelines consistent with our standard DPA.
- Retention & encryption: the 30-day retention window is enforceable if we bind the following to the contract:
  * Customer tenant keys via KMS where feasible (bring-your-own-key recommended).
  * Proof-of-deletion process: we will provide an automated deletion job and periodic audit evidence (hash-based deletion logs) demonstrating snapshot removals.
  * Audit logs: all access to snapshot data must be logged and retained for the same retention period; we can surface audit records on request.
- Implementation notes: for Hosted plans we will rely on our centralized KMS with per-tenant key wrapping; for Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed keys. Hosted support for BYOK is on our roadmap Q2; in the interim we can commit to KMS with restricted access and attestations.

Requested contract language tweaks (legal to incorporate):
- Add requirement that TelemetryStream provides SOC2 attestation and agrees to Redwood's subprocessor security obligations.
- For the retention clause, add that Redwood will provide proof-of-deletion within 10 business days of request and will maintain deletion/audit logs for the retention period.

Given these conditions, Security signs off pending TelemetryStream attestation and inclusion of the two bullets above in the DPA.
